claims.claim: Portugal has a residence visa (the D7) for people living on passive income

sources.name: Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, visas: necessary documentation, residency
sources.says: The residency list has a section "Fixed residency for retirement purposes, religious purposes or people living from passive income"; for retirement it asks for a "Document certifying retirement amount" and for people living from passive income a "Document certifying revenue from movable and immovable property; intellectual or financial assets". The general list also asks for "Proof of financial resources, as defined by decree of the competent government members". The page gives no amounts and does not use the label "D7".

claims.note: The label "D7" is on the consulates' own checklist (see pt-visa-d7-second-adult), not on this page.

claims.claim: The D7 needs at least €920 a month, which is the 2026 minimum wage

sources.name: Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, visas: means of subsistence
sources.says: Means of subsistence are measured against "the minimum monthly salary - currently in 2026 - amounting to 920€", net of social security deductions, citing Regulatory Decree n.º 139/2025 of 29 December; the first adult counts 100%.

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, other taxes
sources.says: "In 2026, the Portuguese monthly minimum wage is EUR 920." Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

sources.name: Garrigues: Portugal, minimum monthly wage increases in 2026
sources.says: Decree-Law no. 139/2025 of December 29th sets the minimum monthly wage at €920.00 from January 1, 2026; "The minimum monthly wage in the autonomous regions of Madeira and Azores is subject to specific ruling." Page dated 01/07/2026.

claims.note: The decree itself could not be read: diariodarepublica.pt returned an empty page, and dgert.gov.pt and aima.gov.pt failed with a certificate error ("unable to verify the first certificate"). The ministry's visa page uses the national €920 for every applicant. A search result, which is not a read, says Madeira set its own minimum wage at €980 for 2026 (Decreto Legislativo Regional n.º 1/2026/M); nothing read says a consulate applies it to a D7 applicant bound for Madeira.

claims.claim: A second adult adds 50% to the required income

sources.name: Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, visas: means of subsistence
sources.says: Per family unit: "First adult 100%; Second adult and additional adults 50%; Children and young people under 18 years of age and non-minor dependent children 30%."

sources.name: Consulate General of Portugal in Manchester: D7 residence visa checklist (PDF, file dated 6 March 2025, hosted by VFS Global)
sources.says: The checklist is headed "Residence visa for retirement purposes, religious purposes or for living from individual revenues (D7)". Means of subsistence are based on the minimum monthly salary, "currently in 2024 amounting to 820€", with "First adult: 100%. Second adult and additional adults: 50%. Children and young people under 18 years of age and non-minor dependent children: 30%".

claims.claim: The income may come from dividends, interest, rent or pensions

sources.name: Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, visas: necessary documentation, residency
sources.says: Retirement: "Document certifying retirement amount". People living from passive income: "Document certifying revenue from movable and immovable property; intellectual or financial assets". Dividends, interest and rent are not named one by one.

sources.name: Consulate General of Portugal in Manchester: D7 residence visa checklist (PDF, file dated 6 March 2025, hosted by VFS Global)
sources.says: "For people living out from personal revenue: Document certifying revenue, made available weekly, monthly or yearly, from movable and immovable property; intellectual or financial assets (dividends, investment portfolio, etc.)", plus a Portuguese bank account; for retirement, a document certifying the pension amount.

sources.name: Portugalist: Portugal D7 visa requirements
sources.says: "Last checked: November 4, 2026." Income that counts: pensions and US Social Security, rental income, dividends and other investment income, interest if ongoing and recurring, and royalties; salary from a remote job and freelancing are sent to the D8, and savings alone do not count unless they produce ongoing income.

claims.note: The official pages name the classes (pensions; revenue from movable and immovable property and from financial assets); the list of dividends, interest, rent and pensions one by one is on the secondary page.

claims.claim: Applicants also show about €11,040 of savings (12 months of the minimum wage)

sources.name: Portugalist: Portugal D7 visa requirements
sources.says: "Last checked: November 4, 2026." Savings of €11,040 for one person, "Proof you can support yourself for at least 12 months" (€16,560 for a couple); it says some checklists require a Portuguese bank account and others only prefer one, and gives no legal source for the savings figure.

sources.name: Consulate General of Portugal in Manchester: D7 residence visa checklist (PDF, file dated 6 March 2025, hosted by VFS Global)
sources.says: Proof of financial resources: "Last 3 months bank statement" and an "Up-to-date bank statement with available funds amounting to at least €9840 (single applicant)", which is 12 × the €820 minimum wage the checklist quotes for 2024.

sources.name: VFS Global Brazil: checklist, visto de residência para reformados, religiosos e pessoas que vivam de rendimentos (PDF, file dated 28 February 2025)
sources.says: General requirement: "Comprovativo de meios de subsistência para um período de, pelo menos, 12 meses, nos termos do n.º 2 do artigo 2.º da Portaria n.º 1563/2007".

claims.note: €11,040 is 12 × €920. The 2026 figure itself is on the secondary page only; the two official checklists read are dated 2025 and give the 12-month rule and the 2024 amount (€9,840). The text of Portaria 1563/2007 could not be read (diariodarepublica.pt returned an empty page).

claims.claim: Draws on a loan do not count as income for the D7
claims.wording: loan draws are not on the consulates' list of income and are believed not to count
claims.oldWording: loan draws do not count as income

sources.name: Portuguese Ministry of Foreign Affairs, visas: necessary documentation, residency
sources.says: The documents accepted for people living from passive income are those "certifying revenue from movable and immovable property; intellectual or financial assets"; for retirees, a document certifying the retirement amount. Loans or borrowing are not mentioned.

sources.name: Consulate General of Portugal in Manchester: D7 residence visa checklist (PDF, file dated 6 March 2025, hosted by VFS Global)
sources.says: The revenue accepted is "from movable and immovable property; intellectual or financial assets (dividends, investment portfolio, etc.)". Loans are not mentioned.

sources.name: Portugalist: Portugal D7 visa requirements
sources.says: "Last checked: November 4, 2026." The lists of income that counts and does not count say nothing about loans, margin loans or borrowing.

also: hedge added ("believed") and the clause reworded to what the official lists show; the unhedged "loan draws do not count as income" is gone
sources: added the Ministry of Foreign Affairs residency visa documents page
claims.note: No page read says in terms that loan proceeds are refused. The official lists name income from property and financial assets and pensions, and a loan is none of these, so the profiles' conclusion is an inference. A search for a page on the point found none. Worth a question to a consulate, since the whole plan rests on living off loan draws.

claims.claim: AIMA processing backlogs are common

sources.name: Portugalist: Portugal D7 visa requirements
sources.says: "Last checked: November 4, 2026." Some applicants get an AIMA appointment booked with the visa; others "don't, and wait months". It reports about 29,000 Golden Visa investors still waiting as of August 2026, and that under Lei 62/2026, in force since 11 September 2026, a renewal is no longer treated as approved because AIMA missed its deadline.

sources.name: Portugal.com: AIMA rejects 23,000 residency applications, continues to work through its huge backlog
sources.says: Dated May 9, 2025. AIMA had approved 123,000 residence permits, 27.5% of 446,921 pending expressions of interest; 117,000 cases were reported as still pending, and the queue still included about 50,000 Golden Visa investors and family reunification applicants.

claims.note: Secondary pages only: aima.gov.pt failed with a certificate error, and two 2026 Portugal News articles (1 July and 9 June 2026) came back empty. The 2025 page gives the scale; the November 2026 page says waits of months still happen. Search results, not read, say the backlog had fallen to about 30,000 cases by July 2026, so "common" may overstate it by now.

claims.claim: Portugal has no wealth tax on financial assets (and its property surcharge, AIMI, does not reach a foreign portfolio)

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, other taxes
sources.says: "There are no net wealth/worth taxes in Portugal." Property: "Municipal property tax is charged on the registered value of real estate." Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do IMI, artigo 135.º-A (Adicional ao IMI, incidência subjetiva)
sources.says: The additional to IMI falls on "proprietários, usufrutuários ou superficiários de prédios urbanos situados no território português"; the article extends it to nothing but real estate.

claims.note: Agrees with LOCAL_TAX_BY_COUNTRY.PT in src/data/localTaxes.ts ("Portugal has no net wealth tax"). AIMI's thresholds and rates were not read, since the profiles do not state them.

claims.claim: Dividends and interest pay a 28% flat rate

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, income determination
sources.says: "Dividends and interest are liable to taxation at a flat rate of 28%." Interest paid by non-resident entities to tax-resident individuals is also taxed at 28%; income paid by entities in blacklisted jurisdictions is "liable to a tax rate of 35% (in 2026)". Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do IRS, artigo 72.º (Taxas especiais)
sources.says: N.º 1 taxes autonomously at 28%, among others, alínea d): "Os rendimentos de capitais, tal como são definidos no artigo 5.º, quando não sujeitos a retenção na fonte"; n.º 18 sets 35% for capital income due by entities in listed low-tax jurisdictions. Last amended by Lei n.º 73-A/2025.

also: sources: the five profiles that cited "PwC: Portugal, taxes on personal income" now cite PwC's income determination page instead; the personal-income page read today gives no rate ("Special rates apply to capital gains and investment income") and nothing on NHR
sources: PwC income determination and PwC other tax credits and incentives added to all six
claims.note: For a US portfolio held at a US broker the income is not withheld in Portugal, so the special rate of article 72 applies, declared in the annual return. Madeira words it "Portugal's 28% flat rate"; see pt-tax-madeira-flat-rate for the regional cut.

claims.claim: The taxpayer may choose the progressive scale instead of the flat rate

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, income determination
sources.says: "the taxpayer may opt to be liable to tax on dividends and interest received at the marginal rates", which it gives as 12.50% to 48% plus the solidarity rate if applicable. Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do IRS, artigo 72.º (Taxas especiais)
sources.says: N.º 13: "Os rendimentos previstos nas alíneas c) a f) do n.º 1 ... podem ser englobados por opção dos respetivos titulares residentes em território português."

claims.note: Madeira's profile does not state the option; it applies there too, on the regional scale.

claims.claim: US tax on the income is creditable in Portugal under the treaty: the profiles said "the 15% US withholding", for dividends and interest alike
claims.oldWording: with the 15% US withholding creditable under the treaty
claims.newWording: with US tax on them creditable up to the treaty caps (15% on dividends, 10% on interest)

sources.name: IRS: Convention between the United States and the Portuguese Republic on taxes on income, with protocol (signed 6 September 1994)
sources.says: Article 10(2): tax in the country of the paying company "shall not exceed 15 percent of the gross amount of the dividends". Article 11(2): on interest it "shall not exceed 10 percent of the gross amount of such interest". Article 25(3)(a): Portugal allows as a deduction "an amount equal to the income tax paid in the United States" on income the US may tax "other than solely by reason of citizenship", up to the Portuguese tax on that income. Article 25(2): for a US citizen resident in Portugal, income the US taxes solely by reason of citizenship is deemed to arise in Portugal to the extent needed to avoid double taxation. General effective date 1 January 1996.

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do IRS, artigo 81.º (Eliminação da dupla tributação jurídica internacional)
sources.says: N.º 1: income obtained abroad gives "um crédito de imposto por dupla tributação jurídica internacional", the lower of the tax paid abroad and the share of IRS on that income; n.º 2: where a convention exists the deduction "não pode ultrapassar o imposto pago no estrangeiro" under the convention.

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, income determination
sources.says: "A credit against the Portuguese tax liability is available for the lower of the tax paid in the foreign country" and the Portuguese tax; for a treaty country the credit cannot exceed the treaty percentage. Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

also: sources: added the IRS copy of the US–Portugal convention to all six
claims.note: Two things were off. The 15% is the treaty cap for dividends; for interest it is 10%. And for a US citizen it is not a withholding: a US broker withholds nothing from a citizen, who pays US tax by return; Portugal credits US tax only up to what the US could charge a non-citizen resident of Portugal (the caps), and the US then credits the Portuguese tax on the rest. The tax score stays 3 (no wealth tax, 28% on dividends). Read from the IRS PDF of the treaty; the Treasury technical explanation was not read.

claims.claim: The NHR regime is closed to new entrants

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, other tax credits and incentives
sources.says: "The NHR regime was revoked with effect from 1 January 2024 onward"; it still applies to those already registered on 1 January 2024 or who met the conditions by 31 December 2023, and to some who became tax residents by 31 December 2024. Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

claims.claim: NHR's successor, IFICI, is for workers, so a retiree has no special regime

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, other tax credits and incentives
sources.says: The tax incentive for scientific research and innovation is for individuals who become tax residents, were not resident in the previous five years, and "carry out eligible activities in eligible entities as defined in the applicable legislation"; it gives a special 20% rate on employment and business income and exempts foreign-sourced income "with the exception of pension income". Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

claims.note: For someone who does qualify, IFICI exempts foreign investment income; a retiree with no eligible activity does not qualify, which is what the profiles say. Madeira's profile says only that NHR is closed.

claims.claim: Madeira cuts the progressive IRS scale by up to 30% below mainland rates

sources.name: AT-RAM (Madeira regional tax authority): Agenda Fiscal, Janeiro 2026 (PDF)
sources.says: "em 2026 a Madeira passa a aplicar o diferencial fiscal máximo de 30% face às taxas de IRS vigente no continente a todos os nove escalões de rendimento, alargando um desagravamento que antes estava limitado aos escalões mais baixos."

sources.name: Simula.pt: IRS Madeira, taxas de novembro de 2026
sources.says: Published 6 November 2026. Decreto Legislativo Regional n.º 17/2026/M, published 5 November, lowers the first six brackets with effect from 1 January 2026 (first bracket 8,75% → 8,54%, against 12,2% nationally) and keeps brackets 7 to 9 at 30,17%, 31,22% and 33,60%; the regional budget for 2026 had already set rates 30% below the national ones.

also: sources: added the AT-RAM Agenda Fiscal of January 2026
claims.note: "Up to 30%" was true until 2025, when the full 30% applied only to the lower brackets. The decree of November 2026 on Portal das Finanças is an image-only PDF that could not be read.

claims.claim: Madeira's cut reportedly does not apply to the 28% flat rate
claims.oldWording: reportedly not to the 28% flat rate
claims.newWording: to the flat rate withheld on Portuguese-paid interest and dividends, but whether they reach the 28% on dividends from a US broker is unverified

sources.name: AT-RAM (Madeira regional tax authority): Agenda Fiscal, Janeiro 2026 (PDF)
sources.says: "Em 2026 mantém-se a redução de 30% das taxas liberatórias em sede de IRS e de IRC para a RAM, face à taxa aplicada no território continental." Its examples are income "obtidos em território português": bank interest, interest on savings and treasury certificates, "Dividendos resultantes de ações".

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do IRS, artigo 72.º (Taxas especiais)
sources.says: The 28% in n.º 1, alínea d) is a special rate charged in the annual assessment on capital income "quando não sujeitos a retenção na fonte", a different provision from the liberatory rates withheld at source under the preceding article. The page says nothing of the autonomous regions.

also: scores.tax stays 3: 28% (or 19.6% if the cut applies) is inside the rubric's 19–30% band
claims.note: The regional tax authority says the 30% cut does apply to the liberatory rates, so a Madeira resident pays 19.6%, not 28%, on interest and dividends paid in Portugal. A US portfolio at a US broker is not withheld in Portugal and falls under the special rate of article 72; no page read says whether the cut reaches it. Consultancy pages found by search (mcs.pt, HTTP 403; not read) appear to disagree with one another. PwC Portugal's 2026 tax guide (pwc.pt, HTTP 403) would settle it. Until then the profile keeps 28% for US dividends and says the point is unverified.

claims.claim: There is no inheritance tax as such: inheritances pay a 10% stamp duty

sources.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Portugal, individual, other taxes
sources.says: "Free acquisition of goods by individuals (inheritance and gifts) is taxed under the stamp tax at 10%." "Donation of property is subject to an additional rate of 0.8%." Last reviewed 03 October 2026.

claims.note: Agrees with LOCAL_TAX_BY_COUNTRY.PT ("its 10% stamp duty on inheritances").

claims.claim: The stamp duty reaches only assets located in Portugal

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do Imposto do Selo, artigo 4.º (Territorialidade)
sources.says: N.º 3: "Nas transmissões gratuitas, o imposto é devido sempre que os bens estejam situados em território nacional." N.º 4 lists what counts as situated there. Last amended by Lei n.º 24-D/2022.

claims.note: Agrees with LOCAL_TAX_BY_COUNTRY.PT ("covers Portuguese-situs assets only").

claims.claim: Spouses, children and grandchildren are exempt

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do Imposto do Selo, artigo 6.º (Isenções subjectivas)
sources.says: N.º 1, alínea e) exempts "O cônjuge ou unido de facto, descendentes e ascendentes, nas transmissões gratuitas sujeitas à verba 1.2" of the general table.

claims.note: The exemption is wider than the profiles say: it also covers a de facto partner and ascendants (parents, grandparents). Children and grandchildren are "descendentes".

claims.claim: US brokerage assets left to US-resident children appear untaxed in Portugal

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do Imposto do Selo, artigo 4.º (Territorialidade)
sources.says: N.º 4, alínea d): shares count as situated in Portugal "quando a sociedade participada tenha a sua sede, direcção efectiva ou estabelecimento estável em território nacional, desde que o adquirente tenha domicílio neste território". Alínea e): money and crypto-assets count when "depositados em instituições com sede, direção efetiva ou estabelecimento estável em território nacional", or, when not deposited, in a succession when the deceased was domiciled in Portugal.

sources.name: Portal das Finanças: Código do Imposto do Selo, artigo 6.º (Isenções subjectivas)
sources.says: Descendants are exempt in any case (n.º 1, alínea e)).

claims.note: Two independent reasons: shares in companies seated outside Portugal are not Portuguese-situs, and children are exempt whatever the asset. The profiles' "appear" may stay. For an heir who is not exempt (a sibling, a friend), US shares and cash deposited at a US broker are still outside the rule as read; cash not held on deposit follows the deceased's Portuguese domicile. No Portuguese ruling on a US brokerage account was read. LOCAL_TAX_BY_COUNTRY.PT models no inheritance tax, which agrees.
